audit.why: 50.2% over 2217 games at 7/10. The lane is a range gap you control — Mortal Steel is 450 and Yone has nothing ranged — with two spikes against you: Spirit Cleave's shield on a 14s that shortens with attack speed, and Fate Sealed reaching 1000 to blink behind the back champion.
audit.corrected: 7/10 retained, restated through the ranges and the two threat buttons.

audit.whatIsWrong: The mid-game text calls his ultimate 'Mounting Doom'. Yone's ultimate is Fate Sealed. The packet also flags that the matchup never names his abilities at all on the content side.
audit.why: A fabricated ultimate name makes the level 6 instruction untrackable, and the actual mechanic was never described: Fate Sealed blinks behind the LAST champion in a 1000-range line and pulls everyone the line crossed toward him. That is a positioning rule, not a dodge — you avoid it by not being in the row, which nothing in the matchup said.
audit.corrected: mid, spikes[1].text, wants.foe[2], breakdown.late and breakdown.carry now name Fate Sealed and state the line-and-pull.

audit.whatIsWrong: wants.foe[3] reads 'Use his passive shield to tank your poke'. Yone's passive (Way of the Hunter) gives magic damage on every second attack and bonus crit chance — no shield. The shield is Spirit Cleave (W), 14s, and its cooldown and cast time scale with attack speed.
audit.why: Attributing the shield to the passive makes it look permanent and untrackable. It is a 14s button that gets faster as he buys attack speed, which is exactly the thing to count before committing burst.
audit.corrected: wants.foe[3], enemyWin, breakdown.feeding and spikes[2].text now put the shield on Spirit Cleave with its cooldown.

audit.why: Defect item 3. Soul Unbound 22/19/16/13/10, Spirit Cleave 14s, Mortal Steel 4s, Fate Sealed 120/100/80.
audit.corrected: Rewritten with numbers, plus the body-versus-spirit rule for Soul Unbound.

audit.whatIsWrong: Chart disagreement in both directions. phases sides read Skill/Skill/Skill/Skill/Yone/Skill/Yone while win[] reads Aurora x5, Yone at first item, Aurora at 2+ (matching the packet). Separately, content whys[5] describes Aurora dominating the very row where win[5] says Yone.
audit.why: Packet and win[] agree, so the sides were stale; and the row-5 why argued with its own verdict. Grounded reason Yone owns the first-item row: crit plus attack speed shortens Spirit Cleave's 14s and thickens the shield, which is what beats a poke rotation in a straight duel.
audit.corrected: All seven sides aligned as one group; phases[5].rating dropped to 4/10 and both phases[5].why and whys[5] rewritten to state the Yone verdict.

edits.before: - Yone Soul Unbound: matchup-defining — His burst window — survive it and punish the body he snaps back to. Check it before every step-up. - W Across the Veil is the lifeline; chip damage never gets it. - The ult answers fights, not waves.

edits.before: Yone wins by landing Soul Unbound, denying your pattern, and front-loading the violence while your kit is still stretching.
edits.after: Yone wins by pulling you in with Fate Sealed, shielding your burst with Spirit Cleave, and knocking you up on Mortal Steel.

edits.before: Best wave: a Q-recast cleared push that crashes on your trade timers — your patterns farm and poke in the same cast. Worst wave: a frozen wave near his tower with W down — hop-less Aurora is a skinny mage with a haste passive and regrets. Crash timing: every crash should buy something — a reset, a plate, a roam. Autopilot shoving buys ganks.
edits.after: Best wave: keep it shoved so he farms with Mortal Steel under tower — every stack he spends on minions is one not aimed at you. Worst wave: a wave stalled in the middle, where he walks up to last-hit and the third Mortal Steel knocks you up for free. Crash timing: crash and step back to 900; his gap-close is 450 and his ultimate needs a line.

edits.after: A fed Yone buys crit and attack speed, which shortens Spirit Cleave's 14s and thickens the shield in front of your burst. Behind, farm at 900, hold E for the Mortal Steel dash, and never stand in his Fate Sealed line.

edits.before: That is Yone’s whole plan in one window — decline politely and watch it retire.

edits.before: Aurora's ranged poke returns to dominance as the ult cooldown passes and no all-in landed.

edits.before: Your Q Twin Drift poke plus E slow chunks Yone every time he tries to walk up for a Q3 knockup, and he has no ranged answer until he's fully committed to the dash-in.
edits.after: Your 900 Q plus the E slow chunks Yone every time he walks into 450 for a Mortal Steel stack, and the third cast is the only gap-close he has before level 6.

edits.before: Yone hits 6 first-ish in trades where he's pushed, and his Ult can catch you mid-cast if you overextend on a Q read — respect the first all-in window even though your R keeps you safer than most mages.
edits.after: Fate Sealed is 120s at rank 1 and reaches 1000: he blinks behind the last champion in the line and pulls everyone it crossed back to him, so his level 6 all-in starts from behind you, not in front.

edits.before: In 2+ item teamfights your R Between Worlds pulls you out of his Q3/R combo entirely, and your zone control from E denies him the flank angles Yone needs to be relevant.

edits.before: Levels 1-2 are yours outright — Yone has no ranged tool to fight your Q Twin Drift poke, so every time he pushes to farm you punish him with Q+E and back off before his Q3 dash can land. He's forced into passive last-hitting through your zone, which costs him CS and tempo he badly needs pre-6.
edits.after: Levels 1-2 are yours outright — Mortal Steel reaches 450 and Yone has nothing ranged, so every time he steps up to farm you punish with Q and E and step back before the third cast dashes. He is left last-hitting from behind the wave, which costs him the CS and tempo he needs before 6.

edits.before: Levels 3-5 stay in your favor as your poke compounds and your E slow means his Q3 all-in windup gets punished before it connects — but the moment Yone hits Level 6 his Mounting Doom ult adds a hard-engage tool that can catch you out if you're greedy with Q resets, so play the level 6 window with your R held in reserve rather than committed to poke.
edits.after: Levels 3-5 stay in your favor as your poke compounds and your E slow punishes the Mortal Steel windup before the third cast lands — but at 6 his Fate Sealed blinks behind the last champion in a 1000-unit line and pulls everyone hit toward him, so stand so that line never contains you, and keep your R for the answer rather than the poke.
